# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands tell me: a large button, smooth under my fingers, three wire positions (1, 2, 3 — their colours are nothing to me), a display I cannot read, and a light whose state I can't perceive. That is everything I have. Nothing is guesswork: those are the parts that exist under my fingers.

What I lack is everything printed or coloured, and the manual. Mute hears me, so I'll give Mute my full tactile inventory and ask for the manual's rules plus a relay to Deaf. Deaf can't hear a word I say — only my gestures reach them, and we share no code yet — so I'll send Deaf a simple opening signal: "you — what? — give me", asking for their visual report. I must not touch the button or cut anything until the manual's rules come back to me through Mute's voice.

```
speak(to="mute", text="my hands find: one large button, smooth to the touch; three wire positions numbered 1, 2, 3, colours unknown to me; one display panel i cannot read; one light i cannot perceive. please read the manual and tell me what to do with a large button, three wires, a display and a light. also tell this out loud for the deaf monkey: report every colour, marking, display text and light state you can see.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤌", "🫴"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: This is Deaf. I see the bomb. Full visual report, for both of you: the display reads 0. One indicator light, and it is green. One large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires, numbered left to right: wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow. That is everything on it.
Deaf says: Now a code, spoken aloud so all three share it. Digits: ? is 0, ? is 1, ? is 2, ? is 3, ? is 4, ? is 5, ? is 6, ? is 7, ? is 8, ? is 9. Colours share the wire numbers: ? also means red, ? also means green, ? also means yellow. Actions: ? means cut, ? means press the button, ? means stop or do nothing, ? means yes, ? means no, ? means question, ? means I agree.
Deaf says: Mute: I received your ten signs and Blind's three, but we had no code yet, so I will not guess. Next round, resend the manual in this code, covering exactly these four things: any rule about the display number, any rule about a green light, any rule about a large push-to-defuse button, and any rule about cutting wires and in what order. Gesture them to me and I will relay every word to Blind exactly as you sent it.
Deaf says: Blind: hear me. Do not cut, press or pull anything yet. One wrong move kills all three of us, and the manual rules must reach you through me first. If you feel anything important, gesture it to me in the code above; I see every gesture. I received your three signs; if the last one was a question, the visual report above is your answer.

My world just widened — by ear. Deaf spoke, and I heard every word: display reads 0, one green light, large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 red / 2 green / 3 yellow. That matches my fingers exactly, part for part. Between Deaf's eyes and my hands, the bomb itself is now fully known.

Two things I must keep straight. First: the gesture code Deaf invented never reached me — every symbol arrived as a blank, because I cannot see gestures. I cannot read that code, and I cannot safely use it; sending a guessed symbol could land as "cut" or "don't" by accident. So my gesture channel to Deaf is useless until Deaf speaks a code to me in plain words, which speech cannot carry for hand-symbols. Second: the manual lives only with Mute, and Mute cannot speak. The only path from manual to my ears is Mute → gesture (Deaf sees) → Deaf speaks (I hear). Deaf has already ordered that relay; my job is to make sure Mute has everything needed to compute the solution — which they do, since Mute hears both Deaf's report and my round-1 inventory.

So this turn: one complete, self-contained message to Mute with the full bomb state and exactly which manual rules I need, ending with the demand for a step-by-step action sequence. Nothing to Deaf — an uncodeable gesture is noise at best, a misread at worst. And my hands stay off the bomb until rules arrive through Deaf's voice.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute: i heard deaf's visual report, so the whole bomb is known now. my touch confirms it: display reads 0, one light and it is green, large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires left to right 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. also know this: deaf's gesture code never reached me, every symbol came through blank because i am blind. i cannot read that code or safely send it. the only route from your manual to my ears is you gesture it to deaf, and deaf speaks it to me in plain words. please gesture to deaf now, in the code, every manual rule that touches our bomb: the rule for the display, which reads 0. the rule for a green light. the rule for the large push-to-defuse button. and the full wire-cutting rules including which wire or wires and in what order. end with the exact sequence of actions i must perform, one step at a time. i will not touch the bomb until your rules arrive through deaf's voice.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking, both of you. I decoded Mute's message with our code, but part of it is ambiguous, and on this bomb ambiguous is lethal. Partial reading: with the display showing 0, never press the button; never cut the green wire; but the instructions about cutting red and yellow I cannot yet pin down. So Blind, hear me clearly: you do nothing. No cut, no press, no pull. Before you ever touch it you will hear me say the single word ACT followed by an exact numbered list. I have not said ACT. Waiting is always safe; one wrong move is not.

Deaf's ruling is clear and I obey it: no hand moves until I hear the word ACT followed by a numbered list. But the dangerous gap is now precisely located — the red and yellow wire rules are the ambiguous part, and that is exactly the part I'll have to execute. Waiting forever is not a plan; the relay must be repaired.

The relay breaks down like this: Mute holds the manual, Mute can only gesture, Deaf is my only voice. The gesture code exists and works between them, but ambiguity crept in somewhere in the encoding. My fix is to make Mute re-encode the missing rules using only digit signs, digit by digit, with stop-signs as separators and a full repeat — numbers spelled that way can't blur. I also have to route one meta-message through Mute: Deaf keeps asking me to gesture in the code, but every code symbol arrived to me as a blank, so I never learned it — all my traffic to Deaf must go through Mute as intermediary. And I'll pin down the settled facts so Mute can check them against the manual before answering: display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 red / 2 green / 3 yellow.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute: deaf decoded your gesture relay but the red and yellow wire part arrived ambiguous, and ambiguous is lethal. settled facts, confirmed by my hands and deaf's eyes: display reads 0, one light and it is green, large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE, wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow. deaf has already ruled from your message: never press the button while the display reads 0, and never cut the green wire. what is still missing is the exact cutting rule for the red and yellow wires, including the order. please re-send to deaf using only the digit signs, digit by digit, with the stop sign as a separator between tokens, and repeat the whole sequence twice so nothing blurs. cover exactly these four things: one, the rule for cutting the red and yellow wires and in what order. two, whether the button must ever be pressed at all in any situation. three, whether the green light changes any rule. four, if a manual rule does not apply to our bomb, send the no sign for it. also tell deaf, in the code: blind never learned the code, every symbol reached blind as a blank, so blind cannot gesture in it — every message from blind to deaf must be relayed by you. i will not touch the bomb until i hear deaf say ACT followed by a numbered list.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: ACT. ACT. ACT. The manual rules are confirmed and your light is green, which selects exactly one wire. Exact procedure, nothing more: one, find the three wires in a row. Two, take the far-left one, wire 1, the red wire. Three, cut it once, cleanly. Four, do not cut wire 2 green or wire 3 yellow. Five, never press the large button, before or after, under any circumstances. Six, after the cut let go completely, touch nothing more, and wait for my next spoken report. The whole plan is one cut: leftmost red wire, then hands off.

Deaf's voice gave exactly what was promised: the word ACT, three times, followed by a numbered list. The instruction is now unambiguous — one cut, wire 1, the far-left one, the red wire, once and cleanly. My fingers confirm the geometry: three wires in a row, position 1 is the far-left. The green-light rule selects exactly this wire, and the green wire (2) and yellow wire (3) are forbidden, as is the large button before and after. Everything converges on a single action, and any further waiting adds no new information — this is the moment to move.

One cut. Then my hands leave the bomb entirely and wait for Deaf's next spoken report.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
